Refactored the package again by pulling the range-aware mutable behavior out of [sorting/InsertionSort.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/035_insertion_sort/sorting/InsertionSort.java:1) into a dedicated internal type, [sorting/IntArraySlice.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/035_insertion_sort/sorting/IntArraySlice.java:1). `InsertionSort` is now just a thin public facade over `sort`, `sortRange`, `isSorted`, `isSortedRange`, and `sortedCopy`, while the insertion-sort mechanics, slice traversal, and copy/sort behavior live in one place.

That reduces duplication around array validation and range handling, and it makes the algorithm code easier to extend without growing the public API class. `IndexRange` remains the validation primitive, and the demo and self-test continue to work unchanged against the packaged API.
